name: Mathematics
tagline: From counting to research mathematics, one card at a time.
description: A complete path through mathematics: school algebra and geometry, the undergraduate major, the graduate core tested on PhD qualifying exams, the main research areas, and today's frontier. It follows the qualifying-exam syllabi of leading PhD programs, with qual-style problems and worked solutions along the way.
notation: ℕ = {0, 1, 2, …}; write ℤ_{>0} for the positive integers. ℤ, ℚ, ℝ, ℂ as usual.
log is the natural logarithm from first-year university on; school tiers write ln and log₁₀.
A ⊆ B is a subset, A ⊊ B a proper subset; Aᶜ the complement; f⁻¹(B) the preimage.
Inner products ⟨x, y⟩ are linear in the first argument (the mathematicians' convention).
Aᵀ is the transpose, A* the conjugate transpose; vectors are columns.
Groups: e is the identity, |G| the order, H ≤ G a subgroup, N ⊴ G a normal subgroup.
Rings are commutative with 1 unless stated; (a) is the ideal generated by a; 𝔽_q the field with q elements.
Measure spaces (X, 𝓜, μ); “a.e.” means almost everywhere; ‖f‖_p the Lᵖ norm.
Topology: int A, Ā (closure), ∂A (boundary); π₁(X, x₀); Hₙ(X; G) with coefficients in G.
Probability: P(A), E[X], Var(X); i.i.d. means independent and identically distributed.
Asymptotics: f = O(g), f = o(g), f ~ g.
